land.text: France with Belgium (1795), the German left bank of the Rhine (1797), Geneva and Mulhouse (1798) and Piedmont (1802): the territory of the Consulate when 'On 18 May 1804, Napoleon was granted the title' of Emperor

predecessors.note: Cliopatria begins the First French Empire in 1805; the page dates the empire to 18 May 1804.

land.text: France in its borders of 1 June 1792 with the additions of the Treaty of Paris of 30 May 1814 (Saarbrücken, Saarlouis, Landau, Montbéliard, part of Savoy, Avignon, the Comtat Venaissin)
'The Netherlands, now freed from the French empire, asked William I' to become their prince; he accepted in late 1813

successors.note: Becomes the United Kingdom of the Netherlands in March 1815 (Treaty of Paris page).

land.text: the Valais, annexed 1810; 'This treaty formally recognized the independence of Switzerland (Art. VI)'

successors.note: Recipient not named by the pages opened.

land.text: the Illyrian Provinces, comprising the Dalmatian coast; French rule ended on 27 January 1814 (Illyrian Provinces page)

successors.note: Austria's formal annexation is dated 9 June 1815 (infobox of the Illyrian Provinces page); the Palatinate also passed to Austria in 1814 (kingdom-of-bavaria gets it in 1816).

land.text: Piedmont, Aosta, Savoy and Nice, returned to the crown in 1814

successors.note: Sardinia gains Liguria only in 1815 (via the Congress of Vienna); see kingdom-of-sardinia /ledger/26, 28.

land.text: Tuscany, re-established under Ferdinand III in 1814
Parma, Piacenza and Guastalla given to Marie-Louise by the Treaty of Fontainebleau (11 April 1814)
Monaco, Menton and Roquebrune, restored in 1814
Catalonia, annexed 1812 to the Treaty of Valençay (December 1813)
Andorra, independence restored by imperial decree in 1814
Hamburg, freed after the abdication in April 1814

successors.note: Oldenburg, Bremen, Lübeck and the Hanoverian north regained their land in 1813 (events in the ledger), before the empire ended.

land.text: Luxembourg, cleared of the French in 1814; the Grand Duchy follows in 1815
the left bank of the Rhine north of the Palatinate, awarded to Prussia (Territorial evolution page)

capitals.name: Paris
capitals.note: Infobox capital 'Paris'. The Senate's decision of 17 February 1810 made Rome 'the capital of Italy' and created the title 'King of Rome'; Paris stays the seat.

rulers.name: Napoleon I
rulers.title: Emperor of the French
rulers.note: Granted the title 18 May 1804, crowned 2 December 1804, abdicated at Fontainebleau on 11 April 1814; back for the Hundred Days, 20 March to 7 July 1815 (infobox).

correction.text: France, Belgium, the Rhine left bank, Geneva, Mulhouse and Piedmont: the 1806 outline without Liguria and without overseas cells

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the empire is proclaimed on 18 May 1804 ('On 18 May 1804, Napoleon was granted the title'); Cliopatria's first shape is 1805. The 1806 outline less Liguria (annexed 1805, Territorial evolution page) and less the overseas cells is the metropolitan empire at its proclamation.

correction.text: the 1806 outline: France, Belgium, Luxembourg, the Rhine left bank, Piedmont and Liguria, without the campaign cells of Germany and Austria and without overseas cells

keyframe_review.note: 733,675 km2 in Cliopatria against 669,579 km2 for the 1806 outline: the extra 200 German and 45 Austrian cells coincide with the Austerlitz campaign area and match no annexation on the pages ('Pressburg: signed 26 December 1805'; Liguria is the one 1805 annexation on the Territorial page). Cliopatria's Senegal, Mauritius and Réunion cells are overseas and are drawn from the first-french-colonial-empire dossier. The infobox gives only 2,100,000 km2 for 1812.

correction.text: the same outline without overseas cells

keyframe_review.note: 675,586 km2 in Cliopatria; minus the overseas cells (Senegal 7, Mauritius 5 and Réunion) about 669,600 km2. Metropolitan content: 'Belgium (1795)', 'the German states on the left bank of the Rhine (1797)', 'Piedmont ... (1802)', 'The Ligurian Republic (1805)', Geneva and Mulhouse (1798).

correction.text: the empire proper: Cliopatria's 1807-1808 shape without Poland, Lithuania, Russia, Czechia, the German states east of the Rhine and overseas cells

keyframe_review.note: 1,049,766 km2 in Cliopatria, 685,061 km2 once the Duchy of Warsaw (969 Polish cells), the German states east of the Rhine (about 490 cells), 19 Lithuanian, 52 Russian and 2 Czech cells and the overseas cells are removed. The Tilsit settlement made Westphalia and Warsaw satellites, not departments: 'Westphalia ... created under the Treaties of Tilsit (7 July 1807)'; the Duchy of Warsaw 'created from the Polish lands in Prussian possession'. They are vassals in the ledger. The French-held Italian cells beyond Piedmont and Liguria (85 cells in 1807) are not dated by the pages (Etruria and Parma 1808) and are kept.

correction.text: the empire proper: France, Belgium, the Rhine left bank, Italy to Rome, the Illyrian Provinces; without Spain, Portugal, Andorra and overseas cells

keyframe_review.note: 1,064,025 km2 in Cliopatria, 790,045 km2 without Spain (1,013 cells), Portugal, Andorra and the overseas cells. Content that the pages date: Etruria and Parma (1808), the Papal States including Rome (1809), the Illyrian Provinces (Treaty of Schönbrunn, 14 October 1809). Spain was Joseph Bonaparte's kingdom ('crowned King of Spain', no year on the page) and Andorra is annexed only in 1812.

correction.text: 130 departments at the peak: France, Belgium, Holland, the Hanseatic coast, the Rhine left bank, the Valais, Italy to Rome and the Illyrian Provinces; without Spain, Portugal, Andorra and overseas

keyframe_review.note: 1,240,343 km2 in Cliopatria (the peak, 1,064,742 for 1812), 853,423 km2 once Spain (1,392 cells), Portugal (66), Andorra and the overseas cells are removed. Holland and the Valais (1810) and the German North Sea coast (1811) are on the Territorial evolution page; the infobox gives 2,100,000 km2 and '130 departments' for 1812, which is 2.5 times the corrected shape and must include the satellites.

correction.text: the empire proper with Catalonia and Andorra, without the Russian front and Joseph's Spain

keyframe_review.note: 1,064,742 km2 in Cliopatria, 886,322 km2 without the 463 Spanish cells beyond Catalonia, the Russian-front cells (Lithuania 77, Belarus 154, Russia 120, Poland 24) and overseas: 'Catalonia and Andorra (1812)' is the Spanish annexation; the invasion of Russia 'began 24 June 1812' and the Grande Armée's ground is occupation, not annexation. Applies to 1812 only.

correction.text: the 1812 corrected outline without the Netherlands

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's 1812 shape runs to 1813. The 1812 corrected outline is kept for 1813 less the Netherlands, 'now freed from the French empire' (William I accepted in late 1813). The rest (Rhine left bank, Italy, Illyria) was lost in 1814. [Repair 2026-11-01: the 1813 outline is the outline at the start of the year less the Netherlands; the 1813 losses of the ledger take effect from their months: the Hanoverian north (October), Oldenburg, Bremen and Lübeck (1813), Catalonia (December).]

correction.text: France within the borders of 1 June 1792 plus the additions of the Treaty of Paris, without Senegal

keyframe_review.note: 504,049 km2 in Cliopatria (499,040 km2 without 5 Senegal cells): France in the borders confirmed by the Treaty of Paris of 30 May 1814 ('France's borders of 1 June 1792 were confirmed', with the additions named). The empire itself ended in April; the shape is France as it stood through the year. [Repair 2026-11-01: between the 1813 and 1814 outlines the ledger now has a dated loss for each block: the Illyrian Provinces (January 1814), Belgium, Luxembourg, Italy per recipient, the left bank of the Rhine, Andorra and Hamburg (1814).]

region.text: France, Belgium, the Rhine left bank, Geneva, Mulhouse and Piedmont

ledger.note: 18 May 1804: Napoleon is granted the title of Emperor of the French. 'On 18 May 1804, Napoleon was granted the title'; crowned 2 December 1804; the empire 'lasted from 18 May 1804 to 6 April 1814'.

region.text: The Ligurian Republic (formerly the Republic of Genoa)

ledger.note: 1805: the Ligurian Republic is annexed. 'The Ligurian Republic (formerly the Republic of Genoa) (1805)'.

region.text: the Ulm and Austerlitz campaigns: the German and Austrian cells of the 1805 shape

ledger.note: 25 September 1805: the Ulm campaign. War of the Third Coalition: the Ulm Campaign ran 'late August to mid-October 1805' ('25 September - 20 October 1805' for the operations); Austerlitz in early December.

region.text: the Ulm and Austerlitz campaigns

ledger.note: 26 December 1805: the Treaty of Pressburg. 'On 26 December 1805, Austria and France signed the Treaty of Pressburg': Austria ceded land to Bavaria, Württemberg and Baden; Venetia went to the Kingdom of Italy.

region.text: the Electorate except the Hanau lands: Napoleon occupied the country and expelled the elector

ledger.note: 1806: France occupies Hesse-Kassel. The page: 'In 1806, William I signed a treaty of neutrality with Napoleon Bonaparte' and 'after the Battle of Jena-Auerstedt, the latter ... occupied his country and expelled him'. No month on the page. Mirror of electorate-of-hesse /ledger/2. The Hanau lands (its /ledger/3, 6) are not mirrored: the page has no sentence on them.

region.text: Saxony, occupied after Jena-Auerstedt

ledger.note: 1806: Saxony is occupied. The page: Saxon soldiers fought against the Napoleonic armies at Jena-Auerstedt; 'After their defeat, the Electorate was occupied and 10,000 Bavarian soldiers and a French city commander moved into Dresden.' No month on the page. Mirror of electorate-of-saxony /ledger/33.

region.text: the whole duchy, 'overrun by the First French Empire'

ledger.note: 1806: French troops overrun Mecklenburg-Schwerin. The page: 'In 1806 the territory was overrun by the First French Empire.' No month. Mirror of duchy-of-mecklenburg /ledger/1.

region.text: the City and Republic of Ragusa, of which General Lauriston took possession

ledger.note: 26-27 May 1806: French troops occupy the republic. Infobox 'Invasion by France: 26 May 1806'; The Times: 'General Lauriston took possession of the City and Republic of Ragusa, on the 27th of May'. Mirror of republic-of-ragusa /ledger/8.

region.text: the German states of the Confederation (Cliopatria outline from 1809; the row starts three years after the treaty)

ledger.note: 12 July 1806: the Confederation of the Rhine under Napoleon as Protector. 'On signing the Treaty of the Confederation of the Rhine, 16 German states joined'; the protectorate 'was a hereditary office of the Emperor of the French'. Westphalia (15 November 1807) and Würzburg (23 September 1806), Saxony (11 December 1806) follow; 'It was at its largest in 1808, when it included 36 states'.

region.text: the Principality

ledger.note: November 1806: the French occupy the principality. The page: 'From November 1806 until the Peace of Tilsit in July 1807, the Principality was occupied by the French.' Mirror of duchy-of-saxe-coburg-saalfeld /ledger/2.

region.text: the city of Lübeck, occupied after the battle of 6 November 1806

ledger.note: November 1806: French troops occupy Lübeck. The page: 'troops under Bernadotte occupied neutral Lübeck after a battle against Blücher on 6 November 1806'. Mirror of free-city-of-lubeck /ledger/1.

region.text: Saxony

ledger.note: 11 December 1806: the Treaty of Poznań. The page: 'On 11 December 1806 Saxony concluded the Treaty of Poznań with France', then joined the Confederation of the Rhine and became a kingdom; the end of the occupation is the reading. Mirror of electorate-of-saxony /ledger/34.

region.text: the Polish lands in Prussian possession, Cliopatria's 969 Polish cells of 1807-1808

ledger.note: 1807: the Treaties of Tilsit (7 July 1807) create the Duchy of Warsaw 'from the Polish lands in Prussian possession' as a French client.

region.text: the Electorate except the Hanau lands

ledger.note: July 1807: the occupation becomes annexation to Westphalia. The page: 'In 1807, with the Treaties of Tilsit, the area was annexed to the Kingdom of Westphalia'; the Fourth Coalition page dates Tilsit '7 July 1807' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_of_the_Fourth_Coalition). Mirror of electorate-of-hesse /ledger/4; the land is Westphalia's, a client of the Empire, not the Empire's.

region.text: the Principality

ledger.note: July 1807: the Peace of Tilsit ends the occupation ('until the Peace of Tilsit in July 1807').

region.text: the Principality of Bayreuth, ceded by Prussia at Tilsit

ledger.note: July 1807: Prussia cedes Bayreuth. The page: 'Occupied by French troops during the War of the Fourth Coalition, Prussia had to cede Bayreuth according to the 1807 Treaty of Tilsit'; it names no recipient, but Napoleon later offered it for sale (see the 1810 loss). Month: Tilsit, 7 July 1807 (War of the Fourth Coalition page). kingdom-of-prussia has no Bayreuth loss in its ledger.

region.text: Western Pomerania north of the Peene, with Rügen, Stralsund and Greifswald

ledger.note: 24 August 1807: Stralsund falls. War of the Fourth Coalition: 'Stralsund fell on 24 August after a siege, thus leaving France in control over Swedish Pomerania'; Swedish Pomerania: 'occupation of Swedish Pomerania by French troops, beginning in 1807'. Mirror of swedish-pomerania /ledger/16.

region.text: the Septinsular Republic, the Ionian Islands

ledger.note: 1 September 1807: Berthier declares the annexation of the Septinsular Republic. The page: 'in the Treaty of Tilsit in July, the Ionian Islands were ceded once again to Napoleonic France', French troops landed on Corfu on 20 August and 'on 1 September ... Berthier as Governor-General declared the annexation of the Septinsular Republic to France'. The septinsular-republic dossier is written by another batch.

region.text: the Kingdom of Westphalia, 'created ... on the left bank of the Elbe'

ledger.note: 15 November 1807: Westphalia joins the Confederation of the Rhine, created under the Treaties of Tilsit (7 July 1807) for Jérôme Bonaparte.

region.text: The Kingdom of Etruria (Tuscany)

ledger.note: 1808: Etruria and Parma are annexed. 'The Kingdom of Etruria and the Duchy of Parma (1808)'; Cliopatria's Italian cells rise to 421 in 1809. [Repair 2026-11-01: region is the gazetteer's Tuscany; Parma is left to the next event.]

region.text: the Duchy of Parma

ledger.note: 1808: the Duchy of Parma is annexed (same entry as Etruria on the page); the counterpart slug is the Cliopatria row that restores Parma in 1815.

region.text: the whole duchy

ledger.note: 1808: Mecklenburg-Schwerin joins the Confederation of the Rhine ('in 1808 Frederick Francis I joined the Confederation of the Rhine'). The page does not say when the occupation ended; the end is bridged here, as in duchy-of-mecklenburg /ledger/2.

region.text: the republic, abolished by Marshal Marmont

ledger.note: 31 January 1808: the occupation ends in annexation. Infobox 'Annexation by Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy: 31 January 1808'; the page has Marshal Marmont's proclamation abolish the republic and merge it into that kingdom, not into the Empire (the Empire holds Ragusa again from 1810: the event of 10 June 1810). Mirror of republic-of-ragusa /ledger/11, which names the Empire.

region.text: Joseph Bonaparte's Spain, a 'Napoleonic client state'

ledger.note: 15 June 1808: Joseph Bonaparte is made King of Spain. The page: 'On 15 June 1808 Joseph Bonaparte, the elder brother of Napoleon I was made King'; infobox 'Client state of the French Empire'. [Repair 2026-11-01: counterpart bonapartist-spain (mirror of its /ledger/1, vassal_start 1808/6) instead of kingdom-of-spain; the date was 1809 at confidence 1 before the page was opened.] Catalonia is left out: it is annexed (1812) in its own events.

region.text: The Papal States, including Rome

ledger.note: 1809: the Papal States are annexed. 'The Papal States, including Rome (1809)'; the Senate's decision of 17 February 1810 'made Rome the capital of Italy' and created the title 'King of Rome' (First French Empire page).

minus.text: the Illyrian Provinces, comprising the Dalmatian coast

region.text: the Illyrian Provinces, comprising the Dalmatian coast

ledger.note: 14 October 1809: the Illyrian Provinces pass to France. They were 'annexed under the Treaty of Schönbrunn, signed 14 October 1809'. The Territorial evolution page lists 'The Illyrian Provinces, comprising the Dalmatian coast' under 1814; it is the only year it gives. [Repair 2026-11-01: Dalmatia, Istria and Ragusa are taken out of this region; they reach the Empire from the Kingdom of Italy in 1810 (event below).]

region.text: Zakynthos and Cephalonia (circles are placements; the gazetteer has no island names)

ledger.note: 4 October 1809: Britain takes Zakynthos and Cephalonia. Septinsular Republic: 'in October 1809 a British expeditionary force under Brigadier John Oswald arrived at Zakynthos' and 'the British quickly occupied Zakynthos and Cephalonia (4 October)'. united-kingdom has no matching event before the protectorate of 1815.

region.text: the Kingdom of Holland

ledger.note: 1810: Holland and the Valais are annexed. 'The Kingdom of Holland and the Valais (1810)'; Louis Bonaparte had been 'installed on the throne of the Kingdom of Holland' (no year on the First French Empire page). Cliopatria's Batavian Republic row runs to 1810 and stands for Holland.

region.text: the Valais

ledger.note: 1810: the Valais is annexed (same entry as Holland on the page).

region.text: Meppen and Dülmen (an 18 km circle at Meppen; Dülmen is a second circle)

ledger.note: 1810: France annexes Meppen and Dülmen. The page: Arenberg was 'mediatised in 1810'; 'France annexed Dülmen and Meppen' (Berg annexed Recklinghausen). Mirror of duchy-of-arenberg /ledger/7.

region.text: the Weser department, capital Osnabrück

ledger.note: 1810: the Weser department leaves Westphalia. The page's department table lists 'Weser | Osnabrück | 1807-1810' and names no recipient; the French Empire is inferred from the cession of Nord and Niederelbe in December 1810 and the annexation of the coast in 1811 (Territorial evolution). Mirror of kingdom-of-westphalia /ledger/6.

region.text: Western Pomerania north of the Peene, with Rügen, Stralsund and Greifswald

ledger.note: 1810: Swedish Pomerania returns to Sweden. The page: 'Under the Treaty of Paris, signed in 1810, the territory was returned to Sweden.' No month. Mirror of swedish-pomerania /ledger/17.

region.text: Biscay, Navarre and Aragon, military governments dependent on Paris

ledger.note: 1810: military governments dependent on Paris. Spain under Joseph Bonaparte, infobox: 'Military governments dependent on Paris (since 1810): Biscay, Navarre and Aragon'. Mirror of bonapartist-spain /ledger/4 (loss to the Empire in 1810).

region.text: the military government of Catalonia

ledger.note: 1810: Catalonia too is a military government dependent on Paris (same infobox); it is annexed in 1812. Reconciles the page's 1812 with bonapartist-spain /ledger/4 (1810).

region.text: Lefkada (circle is a placement)

ledger.note: 16 April 1810: the garrison of Lefkada surrenders. Septinsular Republic: 'The first major military operation was against Lefkada, in April 1810' and 'the garrison surrendered on 16 April'.

region.text: Istria and Dalmatia, with the former Republic of Ragusa

ledger.note: 10 June 1810: Istria and Dalmatia pass from the Kingdom of Italy to the Empire. Kingdom of Italy: 'The final territorial change came into effect on 10 June 1810' and 'Italy lost Istria and the never fully incorporated Dalmatia' (agreed at Schönbrunn, 14 October 1809); Republic of Ragusa: 'In 1810, Ragusa was assigned to the French Illyrian Provinces'. Disagreement: the Ragusa page's infobox has the republic annexed on 31 January 1808 by the Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy, not by the Empire, so the Empire's Ragusa gain is 1810 from italian-republic, not 1808 from republic-of-ragusa (whose /ledger/11-12 name the Empire).

region.text: the Beiras and the Estremadura north of the Lines (Cliopatria's 65 cells, 9.26-6.91 W, 39.07-40.84 N)

ledger.note: August 1810: the French invade central Portugal. Lines of Torres Vedras: the 'loss to the French of the fortress at the Siege of Almeida in August 1810', Buçaco 'on 27 September 1810', 'Massena's forces arrived at the lines on 11 October'. Mirror of kingdom-of-portugal /ledger/32.

region.text: the Duchy of Oldenburg, annexed

ledger.note: 13 December 1810: Oldenburg is annexed. The member table of the Confederation page: Oldenburg 'Annexed by France on 13 December 1810'; 'large parts of what is now northwest Germany were quickly annexed to France'. [Repair 2026-11-01: the old event drew all of Lower Saxony (about 47,600 km2); this one is the Duchy's own outline, Salm is the next event and the Hanoverian north the one after.]

region.text: the Principality of Salm round Bocholt (about 1,700 km2, the area of the District of Borken); the circle is a placement

ledger.note: 13 December 1810: Salm is annexed. The member table: Salm (Salm-Salm and Salm-Kyrburg) 'annexed by France on 13 December 1810'. Principality of Salm: created in 1803, capital Bocholt, 'an area of about 1,700 km2', 'annexed by France in 1811' (a year later than the table). No Salm dossier exists (counterpart given as a name).

region.text: the coastal and northern départements Nord (capital Stade) and Niederelbe (capital Lüneburg)

ledger.note: December 1810: Nord and Niederelbe pass from Westphalia to the Empire. The page: 'In December 1810, the short-lived coastal and northern départements Nord ... and Niederelbe ('Lower Elbe', capital Lüneburg) were ceded to the French Empire.' Mirror of kingdom-of-westphalia /ledger/7; kingdom-of-hanover /ledger/4 records the same land with the Empire as counterpart (a Hanoverian loss, 1813/10 gain), and the 1813 loss below goes to Hanover. Territorial evolution lists 'Hanover' among the 1811 annexations.

region.text: the city of Lübeck

ledger.note: 1811: the occupation turns into annexation. The page says only 'from 1811 to 1813, Lübeck was formally annexed as part of the First French Empire, department of Bouches-de-l'Elbe'; whether troops stayed from 1806 is on no page opened.

region.text: the Free City of Bremen

ledger.note: 1811: Bremen is annexed. Territorial evolution: 'Hanover, Oldenburg, Bremen, and Hamburg (1811)'; History of Bremen: 'Napoleon annexed Bremen in 1811, as capital of the Département de Bouches-du-Weser' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Bremen_(city)). Mirror of free-city-of-bremen /ledger/1.

region.text: the city of Hamburg

ledger.note: 1811: Hamburg is annexed (same Territorial evolution entry). The free-city-of-hamburg dossier starts in 1814, so no dossier holds Hamburg between 1806 and 1811; its /ledger/0 names this Empire as the previous holder.

union.text: the city of Lübeck and its land (298 km2 on the German Confederation page)
Bergedorf, held by Lübeck and Hamburg together until 1868 (a circle; the place is not in the gazetteer)

region.text: the Free City of Lübeck and its share of Bergedorf

ledger.note: 1811: Lübeck is annexed. Territorial evolution: 'Lübeck, on the German Baltic coast (1811)'; Lübeck page: 'from 1811 to 1813, Lübeck was formally annexed as part of the First French Empire'. Mirror of free-city-of-lubeck /ledger/3.

region.text: the Beiras and the Estremadura north of the Lines

ledger.note: April 1811: Massena returns to Spain. Lines of Torres Vedras: 'Marshal Massena ordered a retreat at the beginning of March 1811' and 'returned to Spain in April 1811'. Mirror of kingdom-of-portugal /ledger/33.

region.text: Catalonia

ledger.note: 1812: Catalonia is annexed. Territorial evolution: 'Catalonia and Andorra (1812)'; Spain under Joseph Bonaparte, infobox: Catalonia 'Territory annexed to the French Empire (from 1812 until the Treaty of Valençay in 1813)' and, with Biscay, Navarre and Aragon, under a military government dependent on Paris since 1810 (occupation events above). [Repair 2026-11-01: counterpart bonapartist-spain, whose /ledger/4 dates the 1810 military governments; the annexation itself is 1812.] The Territorial evolution page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Territorial_evolution_of_France) gives the year.

region.text: Andorra

ledger.note: 1812: Andorra is annexed with Catalonia. History of Andorra: 'In 1812-1813, the First French Empire annexed Catalonia', 'divided the region into four départements, with Andorra as a part of the district of Puigcerdà' in 'the new department of Sègre'; Territorial evolution: 'Catalonia and Andorra (1812)'. [Repair 2026-11-01: counterpart co-principality-of-andorra, whose /ledger/5 records the 1812 loss; principality-of-andorra starts in 1814.]

region.text: the military government of Catalonia

ledger.note: 1812: the military government of Catalonia becomes annexation (next events).

region.text: the Russian front reached by the Grande Armée

ledger.note: 24 June 1812: the invasion of Russia begins ('Invasion of Russia: began 24 June 1812'). Cliopatria's 1812 shape reaches 37.7 E; the page says Napoleon entered Moscow without a date.

region.text: the Russian front

ledger.note: 14 December 1812: the Grande Armée leaves Russian territory. French invasion of Russia: 'Beginning on 24 June 1812, the initial wave of the multinational Grande Armée crossed the Neman River' and 'on 14 December 1812, it left Russian territory'; the infobox runs the campaign to 24 December 1812. [Repair 2026-11-01: was 1813 at confidence 1 (page silent); the russian-empire dossier regains the land in 1813.]

region.text: the Kingdom of Holland

ledger.note: Late 1813: the Netherlands are freed. 'The Netherlands, now freed from the French empire, asked William I' to become their prince, and he accepted in late 1813.

union.text: Delmenhorst: 'in 1647 Delmenhorst was finally united' with Oldenburg (Duchy page); Amt Delmenhorst (German Grand Duchy page)
Vechta and the Oldenburg Münsterland: 'By the German Mediatisation of 1803, Oldenburg acquired the Oldenburg Münsterland' (Duchy page); Amt Vechta in the 1824 structure (German Grand Duchy page)
Wildeshausen, an Amt in the 1824 structure (German Grand Duchy page)
Brake and Elsfleth on the Weser, Ämter of the duchy (German Grand Duchy page)

region.text: the restored duchy

ledger.note: 1813: Oldenburg is restored. The page: 'Between 1810 and 1814, Oldenburg was occupied by Napoleonic France'; infobox 'restored 1813-23' for William I. No month. Mirror of duchy-of-oldenburg /ledger/2.

region.text: the free city restored

ledger.note: 1813: the French leave Bremen. The page: 'In 1813, following their defeat at the Battle of Leipzig, the French withdrew.' Mirror of free-city-of-bremen /ledger/2.

union.text: the city of Lübeck and its land (298 km2 on the German Confederation page)
Bergedorf, held by Lübeck and Hamburg together until 1868 (a circle; the place is not in the gazetteer)

region.text: the Free City of Lübeck and its share of Bergedorf

ledger.note: 1813: Lübeck is free again. The page: 'Lübeck reassumed its pre-1811 status in 1813.' Mirror of free-city-of-lubeck /ledger/4.

region.text: the Duchy of Warsaw

ledger.note: January 1813: Russia occupies most of the Duchy of Warsaw. Duchy of Warsaw: 'most of the territory of the Duchy of Warsaw was occupied by Russia in January 1813'; the rest returned to Prussia; the Congress of Vienna formally divided the duchy on 9 June 1815. The page calls the duchy 'formally an independent duchy, allied to France'; the end of French overlordship is dated by the Russian occupation. [Repair 2026-11-01: was 1813 at confidence 1 (page silent).]

region.text: the client state

ledger.note: June 1813: Joseph permanently leaves Spain. The page: 'Joseph permanently left Spain in June' (after Vitoria; he had left Madrid in March 1813); bonapartist-spain /ledger/11 vassal_end 1813/6. [Repair 2026-11-01: counterpart bonapartist-spain; was 1813 at confidence 1.] The Treaty of Valençay of December 1813 restores Ferdinand VII.

region.text: Biscay, Navarre and Aragon

ledger.note: June 1813: Joseph 'permanently left Spain in June'. The page does not say when the military governments ended; the end is bridged at his departure (Vitoria, 21 June 1813, is on the Sixth Coalition and kingdom-of-spain pages).

region.text: the Kingdom of Westphalia

ledger.note: 26 October 1813: Prussian troops occupy Westphalia. Kingdom of Westphalia: 'Prussian troops occupied Westphalia on 26 October, following the French defeat at the Battle of Leipzig on 19 October'; 'The kingdom was then dissolved and the status quo of 1806 was restored'. [Repair 2026-11-01: month and day from the Westphalia page; the Confederation page gave none.]

region.text: the Nord and Niederelbe départements, overrun by Russian Cossacks in October 1813

ledger.note: October 1813: the Hanoverian north is freed. Kingdom of Hanover: 'French control lasted until October 1813, when the territory was overrun by Russian Cossacks'; 'In 1813, George III was restored to his Hanoverian territories'. Mirror of kingdom-of-hanover /ledger/7.

region.text: the German states of the Confederation

ledger.note: 4 November 1813: the Confederation of the Rhine is dissolved. 'The allies opposing Napoleon dissolved the Confederation of the Rhine on 4 November 1813' after Leipzig (19 October 1813); 'Many of its members changed sides after the Battle of Leipzig'.

region.text: Catalonia, annexed until the Treaty of Valençay

ledger.note: December 1813: the Treaty of Valençay. Spain under Joseph Bonaparte: Catalonia was 'Territory annexed to the French Empire (from 1812 until the Treaty of Valençay in 1813)'; the text says 'In December 1813'. The page does not say when French garrisons left Catalonia (the Peninsular War ended 17 April 1814 on the kingdom-of-spain dossier's page); the loss is dated at the treaty.

region.text: Andorra

ledger.note: 1814: Andorra's independence is restored. History of Andorra: 'In 1814, an imperial decree reestablished the independence and economy of Andorra.' Mirror of principality-of-andorra /ledger/0.

region.text: the city of Hamburg, freed in 1814

ledger.note: 1814: Hamburg is freed. War of the Sixth Coalition: Davout 'held Hamburg for France until after Napoleon's abdication in April 1814', the last Imperial field force east of the Rhine. The Empire's end (April) therefore precedes the evacuation by a few weeks; the loss is listed at the end of the empire. Mirror of free-city-of-hamburg /ledger/0.

region.text: the Illyrian Provinces, comprising the Dalmatian coast

ledger.note: 27 January 1814: the last French garrison in the Illyrian Provinces surrenders. Illyrian Provinces: Austria declared war in August 1813; Trieste fell on 29 October 1813, Zara on 6 December 1813, the garrison of Kotor surrendered on 3 January 1814 and that of Dubrovnik on 27 January 1814, 'effectively ending French rule in the Illyrian Provinces'; the infobox gives 9 June 1815 for the formal annexation by Austria (austrian-empire /ledger/7). Territorial evolution dates the provinces to 1814. [Repair 2026-11-01: month and confidence from the Illyrian Provinces page.]

region.text: the Valais

ledger.note: 30 May 1814: Switzerland's independence is recognised ('This treaty formally recognized the independence of Switzerland (Art. VI)'); the Valais, annexed 1810, is lost. [Repair 2026-11-01: dated at the empire's end (April 1814), not at the treaty of 30 May, which the Bourbon successor signed. The swiss-confederation dossier gains the Valais in 1815 from sieben-zenden, so the counterpart pair does not match; kept because no Valais dossier exists.]

region.text: Belgium

ledger.note: Spring 1814: the Low Countries are cleared of the French. War of the Sixth Coalition: on 14 January 1814 Bernadotte's army 'advanced into and occupied the Low Countries'; 'In spring 1814, Bernadotte cleared the Low Countries of the French'. The principality takes Belgium as Governor-General on 1 August 1814 (its /ledger/1, 'Belgium on the left bank of the Meuse', Treaty of Paris); Territorial evolution: the Austrian Netherlands and Liège 'were united with the former Dutch Republic to form a new state, the United Kingdom of the Netherlands' (1815).

region.text: Luxembourg

ledger.note: 1814: Luxembourg leaves French hands with the Low Countries (same pages). Territorial evolution: 'Another new state, the Grand-Duchy of Luxembourg, was created with William I of the Netherlands as its Grand-Duke' (1815). No page opened dates the evacuation of Luxembourg itself.

region.text: Piedmont and Aosta

ledger.note: 1814: Piedmont returns to the crown. Treaty of Paris: 'In Italy, several different political entities were recognized'; the recipients are the restored states (kingdom-of-sardinia /ledger/26, 1814). [Repair 2026-11-01: one event per recipient instead of one loss to Sardinia for all of Italy.] Dated at the empire's end; the treaty of 30 May was signed by the Bourbon successor.

minus.text: the part of Savoy with Annecy and Chambery

region.text: Savoy and Nice

ledger.note: 1814: Savoy (except Annecy and Chambéry) and Nice return to the crown. Treaty of Paris: 'France's borders of 1 June 1792 were confirmed'; Savoy was annexed in 1792 and Nice in 1793, so they fall outside (kingdom-of-sardinia /ledger/28, 1814/5).

region.text: the Ligurian Republic, restored on the fall of Napoleon

ledger.note: 1814: Liguria leaves the Empire; the republic is restored on 28 April 1814 (ligurian-republic /ledger/4), briefly, before the Congress gives Liguria to Sardinia. Treaty of Paris: 'In Italy, several different political entities were recognized.'

region.text: Tuscany

ledger.note: 1814: Tuscany is lost. Treaty of Paris: 'In Italy, several different political entities were recognized'; the grand duchy is re-established under Ferdinand III (grand-duchy-of-tuscany /ledger/2, 30 May 1814).

region.text: the Papal States annexed in 1809

ledger.note: 1814: the Papal States are restored (papal-states /ledger/39). Treaty of Paris: 'In Italy, several different political entities were recognized.'

region.text: Parma, Piacenza and Guastalla

ledger.note: 11 April 1814: the duchies are given to Marie-Louise. Treaty of Fontainebleau: 'Parma, Piacenza and Guastalla ... shall be given, in all property and sovereignty, to her Majesty the Empress Marie-Louise'. The duchy dossier starts in 1815.

region.text: Monaco, Menton and Roquebrune (the circle is a placement)

ledger.note: 1814: the Grimaldi return (principality-of-monaco /ledger/15 dates it 17 May 1814). Dated at the empire's end.

region.text: the left bank of the Rhine north of the Palatinate

ledger.note: 1814: the left bank of the Rhine leaves French hands. Territorial evolution: the left-bank Rhine German states 'were awarded to Prussia' (1815) and 'Saarlouis went to Prussia'; kingdom-of-prussia /ledger/48 gains the Lower Rhine on 9 June 1815. Between April 1814 and the Final Act the land was under allied administration. Saarlouis, Landau and Saarbrücken stay French in the 1814 outline until 1815. Mainz and Worms (Hesse-Darmstadt after 1815) are inside this region: the Hessian share has no dossier yet (grand-duchy-of-hesse is another batch's).

region.text: the left-bank Palatinate

ledger.note: 1814: the Palatinate passes to the Allies. Treaty of Munich (1816): Austria ceded 'the former French arrondissements of Kaiserslautern, Speyer and Zweibrucken' to Bavaria on 14 April 1816 (kingdom-of-bavaria /ledger/14), so Austria held the title; no page opened dates the evacuation or the allied administration (confidence 1).

region.text: the Ionian Islands, Corfu and the remaining islands

ledger.note: April-June 1814: Corfu is evacuated. Septinsular Republic: 'The armistice of 23 April [O.S. 11 April] 1814 obliged the French to evacuate Corfu'; 'In June, Donzelot surrendered the island to Campbell'; the British protectorate follows on 5 November 1815 (united-states-of-the-ionian-islands /ledger/0). Lefkada fell in April 1810 ('the garrison surrendered on 16 April').

region.text: France within the borders of 1 June 1792, with the additions of the Treaty of Paris

ledger.note: 6 April 1814: the First French Empire ends. The page: the empire 'lasted from 18 May 1804 to 6 April 1814'; Napoleon abdicated at Fontainebleau 'on 11 April 1814' and the page's infobox gives 11 April; 'Paris capitulated on 30 March 1814'. France is confirmed within its borders of 1 June 1792 by the Treaty of Paris (30 May 1814). The Hundred Days are not drawn: the page says the empire existed 'again briefly from 20 March 1815 to 7 July 1815'; Hundred Days: Napoleon landed at Golfe-Juan on 1 March 1815, 'entered the capital' on 20 March, abdicated on 22 June after Waterloo (18 June) and Louis XVIII made his public entry into Paris on 8 July 1815 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hundred_Days). The schema has no event for a restoration, and the 1814 outline holds the same land through 1815 under bourbon-kingdom-of-france.

wars.name: War of the Third Coalition

zones.text: the Ulm and Austerlitz campaigns: the German and Austrian cells of the 1805 shape

wars.outcome: French victory at Ulm (October 1805) and Austerlitz (early December 1805); 'On 26 December 1805, Austria and France signed the Treaty of Pressburg': Austria ceded land to Bavaria, Württemberg and Baden and Venetia went to the Kingdom of Italy. Infobox: 11 April 1805 - 18 July 1806.
wars.note: [Repair 2026-11-01] Belligerent habsburg-monarchy (the dossier of the Habsburg lands to 1805/12), not austrian-empire, which starts in 1806. The zone is the Cliopatria 1805 cells that its 1806 shape drops (245 cells of Germany and Austria); the ledger's contest_start/contest_end of 1805 reference it. The war's formal end is the infobox's 18 July 1806; the fighting is 1805.

wars.name: War of the Fourth Coalition

zones.text: the Polish lands in Prussian possession, made the Duchy of Warsaw

wars.outcome: Jena-Auerstedt (1806), Friedland (1807), the Treaties of Tilsit of 7 July 1807: the Kingdom of Westphalia and the Duchy of Warsaw are created.
wars.note: No contest zone is drawn: the pages give treaty results, not the fighting grounds.

wars.name: War of the Fifth Coalition

zones.text: the Illyrian Provinces, comprising the Dalmatian coast

wars.outcome: The Treaty of Schönbrunn, 14 October 1809, gives France the Illyrian Provinces.
wars.note: The page names the treaty but not the campaigns.

wars.name: Peninsular War

zones.text: Joseph Bonaparte's Spain, 'crowned King of Spain'

wars.outcome: France annexes only Catalonia and Andorra (1812); the rest of Cliopatria's Spanish cells are client and occupied ground.
wars.note: The First French Empire page names no war and no dates for Spain; the years are those of Cliopatria's shapes with Spanish cells (1809-1813). [Repair 2026-11-01: Joseph's Spain is bonapartist-spain; see the occupation events of 1810 and the vassal pair 1808/6-1813/6.]

wars.name: French invasion of Russia

zones.text: the ground reached by the Grande Armée to Moscow

wars.outcome: The invasion 'began 24 June 1812'; Napoleon entered Moscow (undated) and the army was driven back.
wars.note: Leipzig (19 October 1813) is dated by the Confederation of the Rhine page only. [Repair 2026-11-01: French invasion of Russia: the army crossed the Neman on 24 June 1812, Napoleon 'moved into Moscow' on 14 September, the army left Moscow on 19 October and 'left Russian territory' on 14 December 1812.]

wars.name: War of the Sixth Coalition

zones.text: Germany east of the Rhine: Leipzig (16-19 October 1813) and Hanau (30-31 October 1813)
eastern France in 1814: the Six Days' Campaign of early February, the capitulation of Paris on 31 March

wars.outcome: Coalition victory: Leipzig (16-19 October 1813), the Frankfurt proposals (November 1813, withdrawn by December), the invasion of France in 1814, the Allies in Paris on 31 March 1814, Napoleon's abdication (11 April 1814 on this page) and the Treaty of Paris of 30 May 1814, which returns France to its borders of 1792. Infobox: 24 December 1812 - 30 May 1814.
wars.note: [Repair 2026-11-01] Zones added: Germany east of the Rhine (1813) and eastern France (1814). No contest events are written for them: six allied states fought, no single counterpart stands for them, and the land lost is carried by the dated losses of 1813-1814. The Treaty of Paris page: armistice 23 April 1814, treaty 30 May 1814.

certainty.note: The annexed departments are administrative lines dated by decree; the client states (Warsaw, Westphalia, the Confederation) have approximate outlines in Cliopatria and are not the empire's land.
The 1812 invasion ground and the shrinking frontier of 1813-1814 are approximate; the borders of 1 June 1792 confirmed by the Treaty of Paris of 30 May 1814 are sharp from the treaty.

notes: TWO CLIOPATRIA ROWS, TWO STATES. 'First French Empire' and 'First French colonial empire' share Wikidata Q71084, but their Wikipedia titles differ (First French Empire; French colonial empire) and the second row is a 438.6 km2 sliver (bbox Wisconsin to Saint-Pierre) that rasterises to no land cells. The First French colonial empire page says the 'first French colonial empire' 'existed until 1814', beginning on 27 July 1605: an overseas empire under successive regimes, not the Napoleonic state. They get two dossiers: this one (metropolitan empire, cliopatria_names only 'First French Empire') and first-french-colonial-empire. Cliopatria's empire shapes contain overseas cells (Senegal, Mauritius, Réunion, Guiana); every correction here removes them, and the colonial dossier carries them. SHAPE SURGERY. Cliopatria's shapes are the empire's zone of control, not its departments: 1805 includes the Austerlitz ground (245 German and Austrian cells), 1807-1808 the Duchy of Warsaw (969 Polish cells) and the German client states, 1809-1813 Joseph's Spain (1,013 to 1,392 cells), 1812-1813 the Russian front (Lithuania 77, Belarus 154, Russia 120 cells). Corrections are written as minus operations on those shapes so the Cliopatria outline of the annexed departments stays; the corrected areas are 0.67 M km2 (1805), 0.69 M (1807), 0.79 M (1809), 0.85 M (1811), 0.89 M (1812) and 0.50 M (1814). The infobox gives 2.1 M km2 for 1812, 2.4 times the corrected 1812 shape and twice Cliopatria's 1.06 M: it must include the satellite states; the dossier treats the 130 departments as the state. NOT FROM PAGES: the Peninsular War, Spain and Warsaw vassal dates (confidence 1, Cliopatria's years), the end of the Russian occupation. DISAGREEMENTS: the end is 6 April (lead) or 11 April 1814 (body and infobox); the North Sea annexations are December 1810 (Confederation page; also the Westphalia page for Nord and Niederelbe) against 1811 (Territorial evolution page); the Illyrian Provinces are 14 October 1809 (First French Empire page) against 1814 (Territorial page's year). The kingdom-of-hanover dossier loses its land to France in December 1810 and to Westphalia in 1807 and 1810, which the Territorial page does not list. HUNDRED DAYS (20 March to 7 July 1815) NOT COVERED: Cliopatria has no 1815 shape and the page budget was five pages; a gap-filler may extend the state or give it to bourbon-kingdom-of-france. The Treaty of Paris of 30 May 1814 returns France to the borders of 1 June 1792; Cliopatria's 1814 shape (504,049 km2) is accepted. COUNTERPARTS: 'Republic of Valais' (1802-1810) has no dossier; 'ligurian-republic', 'kingdom-of-etruria', 'batavian-republic' (Cliopatria's row stands for the Kingdom of Holland), 'duchy-of-warsaw', 'kingdom-of-spain' and 'french-consulate' are other batches' slugs. GAZETTEER NAMES NEEDED: 'Parma' (region: the Duchy of Parma). NOT COVERED (page budget, five pages): the Kingdom of Italy, the Kingdom of Naples, Switzerland (Helvetic Republic), Rome as the 'second city' decree, the Erfurt and Kleve annexations of 1806-1808. REPAIR 2026-11-01 (after the review of eu-20-d): (1) The 1813-1814 collapse now has a dated loss for every block: Illyria 1814/1 (Illyrian Provinces page), Belgium and Luxembourg, Italy per recipient (Sardinia x2, Liguria, Tuscany, Papal States, Parma, Monaco), the left bank of the Rhine (Prussia; the Palatinate to Austria, c1), Andorra, Hamburg, Oldenburg, Bremen, Lübeck and the Hanoverian north (1813), Catalonia (Valençay 1813/12); the losses of April 1814 are dated at the empire's end because the Treaty of Paris (30 May 1814) was signed by the Bourbon successor, not the empire. (2) Oldenburg and Salm are two events (the Duchy outline; a 25 km circle at Bocholt for Salm's 1,700 km2), the Hanoverian north (Nord and Niederelbe, 1810/12) a third, with kingdom-of-westphalia as counterpart; the 1811 annexation is one event each for Bremen, Hamburg and Lübeck. Disagreement kept: kingdom-of-hanover /ledger/4 names the empire as counterpart for the same north, and the Territorial evolution page dates it 1811. (3) Etruria is the gazetteer's Tuscany; Parma is its own event with admin1 Parma and Piacenza. (4) Joseph's Spain is bonapartist-spain (client 1808/6-1813/6; military governments of Biscay, Navarre, Aragon and Catalonia from 1810 as occupations; Catalonia annexed 1812, lost at Valençay 1813/12); Andorra's counterpart is co-principality-of-andorra. (5) Added from neighbours: Ragusa occupation 1806/5-1808/1, Hesse 1806-1807, Saxony 1806, Mecklenburg 1806-1808, Saxe-Coburg-Saalfeld 1806/11-1807/7, Lübeck 1806/11-1811, Swedish Pomerania 1807/8-1810, Portugal 1810/8-1811/4; Bayreuth 1807/7 gain and 1810 loss to Bavaria; the Ionian Islands 1807/9 gain, British conquests 1809/10 and 1810/4, the rest lost 1814; Arenberg (Meppen, Dülmen) and the Weser department 1810. Not mirrored: the Hanau lands of Hesse (the Electorate of Hesse page has no sentence on them), Hamburg's occupation of 1806 (no page opened), the Jura and Geneva (no page opened). Disagreement with the reviewer: the Empire's Ragusa gain is not dated 1808/1 from republic-of-ragusa; the Ragusa page's infobox has the republic annexed on 31 January 1808 by the Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy and assigned to the Illyrian Provinces in 1810, so the gain is 1810/6 from italian-republic (the Kingdom of Italy page: Istria and Dalmatia pass to France on 10 June 1810). (6) Third Coalition belligerent is habsburg-monarchy, with a 1805 zone and contest pair; the Sixth Coalition has zones for Germany 1813 and eastern France 1814 but no contest events. (7) Dates fixed from pages: Russian occupation ends 14 December 1812; Duchy of Warsaw vassal ends January 1813 (Russian occupation); Westphalia falls 26 October 1813. (8) The Hundred Days (20 March - 7 July 1815) are noted on the dissolve event but not drawn (no restore event in the schema). (9) No Hamburg dossier covers 1806-1811. (10) The Ionian Islands resolve to no cell of Cliopatria's 1812 shape, so the corrected outlines do not draw them; the 1807 gain and the losses of 1809, 1810 and 1814 carry them. New gazetteer names: Stade, Lüneburg (places), Bocholt, Meppen, Dülmen (places).
